title: QCDIAG introduction (under GSMTAP type QC_DIAG)
description:
This MR is an initiative to introduce Qualcomm Diagnostic message dissector.

GSMTAP protocol dissector includes GSMTAP_TYPE_QC_DIAG ("Qualcomm DIAG") already.

The new code uses that and registers a new dissector for it.

Introducing QCDIAG dissector:
- based on [Osmocom Wireshak qcdiag branch](https://gitea.osmocom.org/osmocom/wireshark/src/branch/osmocom/qcdiag)
- limited code for first review before adding more
- has a custom dissect function to be able to provide partially decoded packets when the particular message has not been implemented in WS yet (this can be very useful while waiting for additional source codes to be added)
- Some additional comments can be found in the code to have a common understanding what's implemented (since only limited documentation is available in public and some older github codes have some details)
- discussed with Osmocom responsibles about making this code before creating this MR (Harald Welte @laf0rge, Oliver Smith)

Example pcap is attached.
[qcdiag.pcapng](/uploads/96f906317a17ffa9a4043c6291ee7554/qcdiag.pcapng)

This case is slightly different from Length (below). Log Code is included in the packet in some cases (2 bytes) while it is not included in others. That is why I have `logcode_offset`. How would you improve this?

Yes, please submit a new MR for that issue, thanks! Don't worry about the `val_to_str_ext()` issues, that's a pattern that Coverity has trouble with. It's not actually a leak.

Gory details: val_to_str_ext() would leak if the allocator were NULL, but pinfo->pool is never NULL in practice, but we haven't convinced Coverity of that. It happens in a bunch of places, also with some other functions. Maybe if we did something like made `pinfo->pool` a macro and on when compiling for Coverity made it a function that could prove it wasn't returning NULL that would help.
